title: PUT /api/organizations/me does not strip subscription/usage/keycloakOrgId from the request body — a caller with only organization.update can self-modify billing state
description: organization.controller.js updateMyOrg (the self-service PUT /me route, gated only by 'organization.update', not 'organization.admin') builds `update = { ...req.body, updatedBy }` and only deletes update.isActive and update.createdBy before the $set. Its sibling updateById (superadmin-only PUT /:id) additionally deletes update.subscription, update.usage, and update.keycloakOrgId — updateMyOrg does not. Since Organization.subscription/usage/keycloakOrgId have no separate write-protection at the schema level (Mongoose $set on a top-level Mixed-free path just writes it), a caller with organization.update but not organization.admin can PUT arbitrary subscription/usage fields onto their own org document directly, bypassing Stripe entirely.
preconditions: Caller holds organization.update but NOT organization.admin (e.g. a custom role scoped to org profile edits only)
Org currently has subscription.status='trial', subscription.tierCode='growth', usage.users=9, limit.users=10
steps: Call PUT /api/organizations/me with body { subscription: { status: 'active', tierCode: 'enterprise', frameworkLimit: -1 }, usage: { users: 0 } }
Call GET /api/organizations/me and inspect subscription and usage
expectedResult: Current behavior: the request succeeds (200) and subscription.status/tierCode/frameworkLimit and usage.users are overwritten exactly as sent — no Stripe webhook, no payment, no organization.admin check. This is a billing-bypass / privilege-escalation gap that should be flagged for remediation (strip subscription/usage/keycloakOrgId in updateMyOrg exactly as updateById already does).

title: PUT /api/organizations/me does not strip licensedFrameworks — a caller with only organization.update can self-grant framework licenses
description: Same root cause as ORGM-SEC-001 (updateMyOrg's incomplete strip-list versus updateById), but a distinct exploit surface: licensedFrameworks is the field updateLicensedFrameworks (superadmin-only, requirePermission('organization.admin')) exists specifically to gate, with cascade logic to revoke/reactivate ClientFrameworks. Writing it directly through PUT /me bypasses that entire superadmin-only control and its cascade side effects.
preconditions: Caller holds organization.update but NOT organization.admin
Org's licensedFrameworks is currently a restrictive whitelist not including framework X
steps: Call GET /api/organizations/:id/licensed-frameworks (or GET /me) and inspect licensedFrameworks
expectedResult: Current behavior: licensedFrameworks is overwritten to the attacker-supplied list with no ID validation (unlike the dedicated endpoint, which validates each ID against ComplianceFramework) and no organization.admin check — a self-service field write silently grants access to frameworks the org never licensed. Should be flagged for remediation.

title: GET /api/users/:id rejects a request for a user ID belonging to a different organization
description: Route-level IDOR regression guard for assertOrgAccess (user.controller.js) — an org admin (organization.admin=false) attempting to read a user in another tenant's org must be rejected and the attempt logged as authz.cross_org.attempt, not merely return an empty/filtered response.
preconditions: Two orgs (A, B) each with at least one active user
Valid JWT for an org A admin (not a platform superadmin)
steps: As an org A admin, call GET /api/users/:id using a userId that belongs to org B
expectedResult: 403 Forbidden 'Access denied' — no PII (email, name, roles) belonging to the org B user is returned in the response body. A structured 'authz.cross_org.attempt' log entry is emitted with requestingOrgId and targetOrgId.

title: POST /api/users rejects extraPermissions the caller does not themselves hold, end-to-end through the real route and JWT
description: Route-level regression guard for assertGrantablePermissions (unit-tested in isolation as ORGM-UNIT-006). Confirms the full path — real JWT, real requirePermission('user.create') middleware, real req.permissions Set built from Redis/DB — actually rejects the escalation attempt rather than only the function-level mock.
preconditions: Caller (User A) holds only ['user.create', 'evidence.read'] — no organization.admin, no billing.admin
steps: As User A, call POST /api/users with a valid new-user payload plus extraPermissions: ['organization.admin']
expectedResult: 403 'You cannot grant permissions you don't have: organization.admin' — no User document is created (not even with the disallowed permission stripped; the whole request is rejected). A structured 'authz.privilege_escalation.attempt' log entry is emitted with User A's id and orgId.

title: System roles cannot be modified or deleted via the Roles API regardless of caller permissions
description: role.controller.js update()/remove() both check role.isSystem and throw a 400 before any org-ownership or field-level checks run, and role.model.js's pre('save') hook is a second line of defense (ORGM-UNIT-003) if a controller-level check is ever bypassed. This case verifies the API-level guard for both the 'Org Admin' (SUPERADMIN) system role and a caller who holds role.update/role.delete but is not the platform superadmin.
preconditions: Target roleId is the system 'Org Admin' role (isSystem=true, systemRoleKey='SUPERADMIN')
steps: Call PUT /api/roles/:id (system role id) with body { description: 'tampered' }
Call DELETE /api/roles/:id for the same system role id
expectedResult: Both calls return 400 ('System roles cannot be modified.' / 'System roles cannot be deleted.') — the Role document is byte-for-byte unchanged in the database after either call.

title: PUT /api/users/:id/roles rejects a roleId belonging to a different organization's custom role, at the real route
description: Route-level regression guard for validateRoleIds (unit-tested in isolation as ORGM-UNIT-007). Confirms the cross-org custom-role reference is rejected before any User.roleIds write, using the real assignRoles controller path (requires user.admin) rather than calling the helper function directly.
preconditions: Org B has a custom role 'Contractor' (organizationId = org B)
Caller is an org A admin with user.admin, targeting an org A user
steps: As the org A admin, call PUT /api/users/:targetUserId/roles with body { roleIds: ['<orgB-contractor-role-id>'] }
expectedResult: 400 Bad Request — 'Role "Contractor" does not belong to this organization.' The target user's roleIds field is unchanged; no cross-org role reference is ever persisted.
